Verification status

Modules verified: a 45-check end-to-end test of the six modules passes (dataset integrity, preprocessing options, classification, indexing, BM25, phrase and negation queries, rank fusion, ranking comparison, the four-method evaluation, all three recommender approaches, and exact/near-duplicate detection).

Front end rewritten: app.py now drives every stage of the IR lifecycle and calls the new module APIs. The Evaluation Dashboard bug is fixed — runs are recorded with the real document ids returned by the search engine rather than range(len(results)), so the reported Precision, Recall, F1, MAP, MRR and NDCG are now meaningful.

Still outstanding: README.md needs the dataset description, findings tables and reproduction instructions.

search_engine.pyWeb Searching (4 marks)

Results now carry doc_id and metadata titles; added BM25, query operators, pseudo-relevance feedback and min-max normalised rank fusion; hardened HITS and the score visualisations; added a rank-comparison table and index statistics.

17def normalize_scores(scores: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
18    """Min-max normalise a score vector onto [0, 1].
19 
20    Text similarity lies in [0, 1] while PageRank sums to 1 over all nod
 >es
21    (so individual values are ~1/N). Fusing the two without normalisatio
 >n lets
22    the text score dominate completely, which makes the link-analysis
23    contribution invisible. Both components are therefore rescaled first
 >.
24    """
25    scores = np.asarray(scores, dtype=float)
26    if scores.size == 0:
27        return scores
28    lowest, highest = float(scores.min()), float(scores.max())
29    if highest - lowest < 1e-12:
30        return np.zeros_like(scores)
31    return (scores - lowest) / (highest - lowest)

120    def _bm25_scores(self, query_terms: List[str]) -> np.ndarray:
121        """Score every document against the query terms with Okapi BM25.
 >"""
122        n_docs = self.term_frequencies.shape[0]
123        scores = np.zeros(n_docs, dtype=float)
124        vocabulary = self.count_vectorizer.vocabulary_
125 
126        for term in query_terms:
127            column = vocabulary.get(term)
128            if column is None:
129                continue
130            term_freq = np.asarray(self.term_frequencies[:, column].tode
 >nse()).ravel().astype(float)
131            denominator = term_freq + self.bm25_k1 * (
132                1 - self.bm25_b + self.bm25_b * self.doc_lengths /
133                (self.avg_doc_length if self.avg_doc_length else 1.0)
134            )
135            scores += self.bm25_idf[column] * (term_freq * (self.bm25_k1
 > + 1)) / np.where(
136                denominator == 0, 1e-12, denominator)
137 
138        return scores

140    def parse_query(self, query: str) -> Dict:
141        """Parse a query into free text, required terms, excluded terms 
 >and phrases.
142 
143        Supported syntax:
144            "exact phrase"   the phrase must occur verbatim in the docum
 >ent
145            +term            the term must occur in the document
146            -term            the term must not occur in the document
147        """
148        phrases = re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', query)
149        remainder = re.sub(r'"[^"]+"', ' ', query)
150 
151        required, excluded, free_terms = [], [], []
152        for token in remainder.split():
153            if token.startswith('+') and len(token) > 1:
154                required.append(token[1:].lower())
155            elif token.startswith('-') and len(token) > 1:
156                excluded.append(token[1:].lower())
157            else:
158                free_terms.append(token)
159 
160        free_text = ' '.join(free_terms + phrases + required)
161        return {
162            'raw': query,
163            'free_text': free_text.strip(),
164            'phrases': [phrase.lower() for phrase in phrases],
165            'required': required,
166            'excluded': excluded
167        }

 >ravel()

23def safe_df_bounds(n_docs: int) -> Tuple[int, float]:
24    """Return (min_df, max_df) that are safe for the size of the collect

27

29       ``ValueError: max_df corresponds to < documents than min_df`` on 
 >tiny
30       collections, which is exactly what happens after a shallow crawl.
31    2. More subtly, ``min_df=2`` deletes every term that occurs in only 
 >one
32       document. Those terms are the *most* discriminative ones for retr
 >ieval,
33       so queries for them silently return zero results. Rare terms are
34       therefore kept for any collection small enough for it to matter.

36    if n_docs < 50:
37        return 1, 1.0
38    return 2, 0.95

12def normalize_scores(scores: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
13    """Min-max normalise a score vector onto [0, 1] for fair fusion."""
14    scores = np.asarray(scores, dtype=float)
15    if scores.size == 0:

17    lowest, highest = float(scores.min()), float(scores.max())
18    if highest - lowest < 1e-12:
19        return np.zeros_like(scores)
20    return (scores - lowest) / (highest - lowest)

evaluation_metrics.pyEvaluation Metrics (1.5 marks)

web_crawler.pyCrawling requirements (Section B)

The stay-on-domain option is now enforced, duplicate-URL and depth-limited counters are separated, shingle-based near-duplicate detection was added, and non-crawled sources can be ingested through the same duplicate policy.

app.pyStreamlit workflow (2 marks)

Rewritten end to end: staged session state with downstream invalidation, three acquisition modes (crawl, bundled corpus, upload) with a tunable near-duplicate threshold, preprocessing options that are actually honoured, BM25 and query operators in the search page, a rank-comparison view, content/collaborative/hybrid recommendation, and an Evaluation Dashboard that uses real retrieved document ids instead of rank positions.

 > positions, "

 >on.\n\n"
1634            "**Recommendation.** A near duplicate is the nearest neighbo
 >ur of its "
1635            "own original, so the Top-K list degenerates into copies of 
 >the seed "
1636            "document.\n\n"
1637            "**Evaluation.** Precision@K is inflated when a duplicate of
 > a relevant "
1638            "document counts as a second hit, and judgements made on one
 > copy do "
1639            "not transfer to the other, so scores become unstable.\n\n"
1640            "**Mitigation implemented here.** MD5 content hashing remove
 >s exact "
1641            "duplicates; 5-shingle Jaccard similarity above a configurab
 >le "

 >visited "

 >t handles "

 >s the text: "

 >ad.\n\n"

 >item whose "

 > captures "

 >start items "

 >"
1665            "**When to prefer which.** Use content-based for a fresh or

 >nse "

 > get "
